title: Checking an infusion pump before and after a change
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.
The exercise has not been tested with learners, and its Arabic version has not been written.
The order of the steps is the author's choice; the source lists the checks without a strict sequence.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
objectives: Know the checks that keep an infusion pump safe when something changes.

sources.use: FDA infusion pump page: verify, label, use the library, respond to alerts, report
ISMP high-alert list: used only to say that some medicines need extra care

required_sources: The unit's pump procedure and drug-library policy
Manufacturer instructions for the pump in use
setup: A fictional pump on a fictional ward; no drug or rate is named.

steps.text: Label the pump channel and the tubing with the name of the fluid or drug if the pump does not show it
steps.why: Labels at the port of entry help others identify what is running.

steps.text: Check the programming against the order
steps.why: The settings must match what was prescribed.

steps.text: Use the drug library if one exists
Respond carefully to any alert rather than silencing it
Stop and report an alert you cannot resolve or a mismatch with the order
